The full population distributions highlight differences between disparity at the extremes (e.g., 90th percentile) and at the mean. Additionally, the selection of study geography and reference population can influence the magnitude and relative ordering of exposure disparities. Thus, methodological choices can lead to different conclusions for the same concentration and population surfaces; this can impact not only the findings of an individual study but also have implications for mitigation strategies. We conclude with recommendations for best practices for making, justifying, and communicating these methodological decisions.

papers.title: Unified Graph-based Interatomic Potential for Perovskite Structure Optimization
papers.abstract: Halide perovskites (HaPs) hold immense potential for applications such as optoelectronics and catalysis. Their vast compositional space, spanning bulk alloys, defects, impurities, surfaces, and surface defects, poses significant challenges for efficient exploration and optimization. To address this, we trained a unified graph-based deep learned interatomic potential capable of optimizing and predicting energetics across these diverse structural motifs and navigating the complex potential energy surface (PES). Using a comprehensive density functional theory dataset of HaP structures, which includes bulk alloys, native and impurity defects, and surface slabs, we rigorously trained and benchmarked the M3GNet-based machine learning interatomic potential (IAP). The M3GNet-IAP framework, trained on DFT-calculated energies, forces, and stresses, enables gradient-based optimization and efficient exploration of the PES. Our models, trained on a dataset of∼12,000 HaP structures across diverse structural do- mains, demonstrated robust generalizability across the complex PES, achieving low er- rors (energies(E): 3.7 meV/atom; forces(f): 16.5 meV/Å; stresses(σ): 5.5 MPa), and accurately predicting formation energies, decomposition energies, defect energies, and surface energies. Our unified surrogate model provides a holistic approach to geometry optimization across different structural variations in HaPs and will be transformative for the discovery of promising new compositions, important defects and dopants, and surface properties.

papers.title: Uncovering Internal Prediction Mechanisms of Transformer-Based Chemical Foundation Models
papers.abstract: Supervised deep learning has become a standard approach to deliver competitive predictive tools that allow relating the structure of molecules and their physicochemical features to properties such as binding to protein targets, performance as electronic materials, and reactivity. However, efforts to understand how these models learn and how specific predictions can be explained are still limited in chemistry, which hinders trust in these predictions. To overcome both the current widespread approach of considering supervised deep learning models as black boxes and the limitations of explainable deep learning based on feature attribution, we introduce two general methods from the field of mechanistic interpretability to molecular property prediction. Specifically, we leverage ablation and adapt existing techniques into the regression lens to inspect model predictions of the Transformer-based ChemBERTa foundation model. Our results for 3 ChemBERTa-based models finetuned on distinct datasets allow us to propose the internal mechanisms operable within each of the corresponding model layers that lead to the final predictions. Our results are a stepping stone towards more trustworthy deep learning models in the molecular domain.

papers.title: Blunt-Force Assembly: Programmable DNA Architectures using π–π Stacking
papers.abstract: Sticky-ended cohesion has been the driving force for DNA self-assembly and has enabled model and design programmability in DNA nanotechnology for over 40 years. Traditional units within self-assembled crystals have rationally-designed sticky ends to avoid unpredictable packing behavior, but in doing so, the surprising variety of contact flavors available to natural nucleic acids remains unexploited. Here, we employ composable DNA tiles to form complex 3D architectures using blunt-ended motifs with single duplex interfaces, leveraging the geometry of the tile and the terminal nucleobase identity to control self-assembly outcomes. We establish programmability and tunable packing, obtaining both unusual and fundamental assemblies, including translational and inversion symmetries at the blunt ends, both 5'-3' and 5'-5' stacking, and both positive and negative twist values. These motifs self-assemble into seven crystallographic space groups, achieving diffraction from 1.86 to 10.0 Å. Finally, we establish the ability of racemic mixtures of L- and D- DNA motifs to perform programmable co-assembly driven by terminal π–π interactions, demonstrating molecular recognition and coexistence between mirror molecular systems. In sum, we demonstrate the ability to tune and program supramolecular assemblies of DNA relying solely on sequence-driven aromatic stacking and tile shape, obviating the need for hydrogen bond recognition between subunits.

papers.title: Concise Synthesis of Advanced Glycation Endproduct Derived from Arginine for Use in Solid-Phase Peptide Synthesis
papers.abstract: Advanced glycation end products (AGEs) contribute to Diabetes and neurodegenerative diseases like Alzheimer’s disease by structurally diverse class of post-translational protein modifications prevalent but the mechanisms involved are not clear. Targeting AGEs has potential therapeutic implication. This protein glycation is produced through nonenzymatic reactions of arginine or lysine with glucose-derived alpha-dicarbonyl compounds. Glyoxal—a two carbon dialdehyde—is the smallest of this class and generates carboxymethyllysine (CML) from lysine, and Glarg with arginine. While CML modifications in proteins are frequently identified, observations of Glarg are relatively scarce as the imidazolone ring readily hydrolyzes to carboxymethylarginine (CMA) under harsher conditions. To better understand the impact of Glarg modifications on Alzheimer’s disease, we elucidate the mechanism of synthesizing the AGEs Glarg and protein with well-defined AGEs. The result indicated that the synthesized AGEs, Glarg hydrolyzed to CMA. We envision that this research will help provide new insights into the structural and functional impact of these protein modifications.

papers.title: Towards Inline Ultrasonic Characterisation of Battery Slurry Mixing: Opportunities, Challenges, and Perspectives
papers.abstract: Inefficiencies in the slurry mixing stage are a major factor in high scrap rates in battery manufacturing, thus hindering sustainable production. Current offline characterisation techniques for slurry microstructure and rheology are slow and inadequate for closed-loop quality control or process optimisation. This review evaluates ultrasound as a promising inline, non-invasive characterisation tool to address this crucial need. We critically examine decades of developments and applications in ultrasonic evaluation techniques, assessing their relevance and identifying challenges specific to the high-concentration, non-Newtonian battery slurries. Key wave-slurry interaction mechanisms, including attenuation, wave speed, scattering, and guided wave propagation, are discussed in the context of characterising microstructural features (e.g. particle dispersion and agglomeration) and macroscopic rheological properties (e.g. viscosity and viscoelasticity). To make full use of the crucial yet limited information accessible via ultrasound, we propose a hybrid framework marrying ultrasonic and other offline data through physics-informed machine learning for accurate and comprehensive property estimation. With the analyses and framework, this review points to a clear path towards achieving robust inline monitoring and efficient optimisation of battery slurry mixing.

papers.title: Conceptual Framework for Innovating Non-Biological Drugs with 200-Fold Superior Efficacy and Safety Over Biologics in Oncology
papers.abstract: This conceptual framework proposes an out-of-the-box approach to innovate non-biological drugs that surpass biologics by 200-fold in efficacy and safety for cancer treatment. Integrating advanced paradigms from physics, chemistry, medicine, biology, engineering, and materials science, we delineate a multi-dimensional strategy leveraging quantum-inspired molecular design with Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE) computations, nanotechnology-enhanced delivery systems with EPR effect, and AI-driven optimization including Bayesian neural networks for personalized medicine. Rigorous mathematical derivations, including multi-compartment pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) models, enhanced Bayesian inference with advanced MCMC techniques for uncertainty quantification, therapeutic index calculations, advanced global sensitivity analyses using Sobol indices and δ measures, and sensitivity analyses, underpin the framework. Realistic simulations via Python code demonstrate reproducibility and falsifiability, with extended time scales showing sustained efficacy. Supported by recent peer-reviewed references from prestigious journals, this self-contained theoretical manuscript advances oncology drug development.

papers.title: Mechanistic Insights into Catalytic Hydrosilylation of Carbonyl Compounds versus [2+2] Cycloaddition Pathway Mediated by Germylyne Complexes
papers.abstract: A cooperative mechanism has been proposed for the catalytic hydrosilylation of aldehydes and ketones mediated by a molybdenum germylyne complex Cp*(CO)₂Mo≡GeC(SiMe₃)₃, based on density functional theory (DFT) calculations and kinetic studies. The computational results revealed a non-classical pathway involving a six-membered-ring transition state at the rate-determining step, underscoring the pivotal role of the polarized metal-germanium multiple bond. In this mechanism, the hydrosilane and aldehyde are partially activated at the metal and germanium centers, respectively. The hydride transfer from the Si-H bond of the hydrosilane to the carbonyl carbon occurs cooperatively in a concerted fashion, bypassing SiH oxidative addition. The activation parameters calculated for this pathway are consistent with those obtained from Eyring analysis of the catalytic hydrosilylation of benzaldehyde with triethylsilane in the presence of the molybdenum germylyne complex. Furthermore, the [2+2] cycloaddition pathway, which was previously observed for the tungsten analogue in reactions with aldehydes but absent in the molybdenum system, was also investigated theoretically, revealing a metal-dependent pathway-switching process governed by the identity of the central metal.

papers.title: Possible bond character effect on self-healing properties of materials for sustainable energy conversion
papers.abstract: Sustainability of energy conversion materials depends on their functional resilience. Such can be achieved by self-healing, SH, which requires mass transfer inside the material. Unfortunately, we lack guidelines as to which physical and chemical material properties can help predict if a material can self-heal and how. We report a data-driven approach to find such properties, using experimental and computational data from materials databases. We focus on four properties: optical deformation potential (ODP), relative structural polarization (RSP), ionicity, and hardness to distinguish SH materials from others. ODP with RSP predict the two main SH mechanisms in semiconductors: mass transfer of kinetically stabilized (class I) or thermodynamically stabilized (class II) defects. In crystals with covalent bonding, the correlation of hardness with ionicity & RSP emphasizes effects of the nature of the chemical bonding on the SH mechanism. Our approach and results present first steps to find SH materials, especially for energy conversion.

papers.title: One-dimensional van der Waals Porous Fibrils Assembled from Metal-organic Polyhedra
papers.abstract: Supramolecular systems exhibit collective functions that emerge from the hierarchical assembly of individual molecular building blocks. Metal–organic polyhedra (MOPs) are a class of functional supramolecular architectures with well-defined molecular geometry and an intrinsic cavity. In recent years, considerable progress has been made in assembling MOPs into extended networks to create porous solids; however, most reported MOP assemblies are limited to three-dimensional networks, which, owing to their high-dimensional connectivity, hinder effective stress dissipation and make them brittle under mechanical stress. Here, we report the one-dimensional (1D) self-assembly of MOPs into supramolecular polymeric aerogels that combine permanent microporosity with exceptional mechanical flexibility. The reaction between amino acid-functionalized naphthalenediimide (NDI) linkers and copper salts led to the synthesis of octahedral copper-based MOPs, followed by their spontaneous self-assembly to form supramolecular gels. The corresponding aerogels converted from the gels by supercritical carbon dioxide drying possessed uniform 1D fibrillar networks (14.8 ± 2.2 nm in width) with intrinsic microporosity derived from individual MOP cavities. The aerogel endured 87% compressive strain without fracture, demonstrating distinct ductility. Furthermore, these fibrils in the supramolecular gels were converted to crystals after two weeks. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction (SC-XRD) revealed that MOPs are arranged via face-to-face interaction between octahedral MOPs to form a 1D helical chain structure. An analysis of the self-assembly process using Hansen solubility parameters unveiled that solvent conditions with high polarity and low dispersion interaction drive the formation of anisotropic assemblies. This work provides a new strategy for tailoring the mechanical properties of supramolecular materials through dimensional control of their assemblies.

papers.title: Electrolyte Effects on Disorder-enhanced Capacitance in Nanoporous Carbons
papers.abstract: The impact of pore structure and surface functionality on the capacitance of nanoporous carbons has been widely studied across different electrolytes, yet the role of electrolyte chemistry in structural disorder-driven and ion adsorption capacity-related capacitance remains largely unexplored. In this study, we investigate the relationship between capacitance and the degree of structural order in 20 nanoporous carbons using ionic liquid electrolytes, aiming to establish the generality of disorder-driven capacitance and explore its underlying mechanisms. Our results demonstrate that carbons with smaller graphene-like domains and larger ion adsorption capacities exhibit higher capacitance in 1-ethyl-3-methylimidazolium tetrafluoroborate (EMIBF₄) ionic liquid, consistent with our previous findings in 1 M tetraethylammonium tetrafluoroborate (TEABF₄). More generally, we find that the capacitance of a given carbon remains similar across different ionic liquid and organic electrolytes, provided that the pores are accessible to the electrolyte ions. This study shows the generality of disorder-driven and adsorption-dependent capacitance in nanoporous carbons in organic and ionic liquid systems and suggests that quantum capacitance may play an important role in disorder-driven capacitance, providing insights for designing high-performance supercapacitor electrodes.

papers.title: Synthesis and Uranium(VI) Extraction Performance of a Calix[4]pyrrole–Tetrahydroxamic Acid Receptor
papers.abstract: The contamination of water by uranium poses a serious threat to ecosystems and human health, creating a need for efficient and selective remediation strategies. Supramolecular materials, with their pre-organized structures, offer a promising route for uranium removal. Phenoxycalix[4]pyrroles are well-known supramolecular scaffolds capable of selective metal binding, making them attractive candidates for designing uranium extractants. Here, we report the design and synthesis of PCP HA, a phenoxycalix[4]pyrrole scaffold functionalized with four hydroxamic acid groups, and evaluate its uranium(VI) extraction potential. PCP HA was synthesized from its ester precursor (PCP E) via hydroxyaminolysis using KOH, achieving a 95% yield. Its structure was confirmed by 1H NMR, 13C NMR, and HRMS. The uranium(VI) extraction efficiency of PCP HA was evaluated by solid–liquid extraction experiments, with measurements performed by gamma spectroscopy. PCP HA demonstrated good performance, removing up to 95% of uranium(VI) from aqueous solutions (1mM) at pH 3, likely due to the strong coordination provided by its hydroxamic acid groups. Further studies revealed that the extraction efficiency also depends on the ligand-to-metal molar ratio. These findings establish PCP HA as a promising supramolecular material for the removal of uranium(VI) from aqueous media.

papers.title: Eliminating air pollution disparities requires more than emission reduction
papers.abstract: In the United States, people of color are disproportionately and unjustly exposed to air pollution. Historically, environmental policy has emphasized aggregate emission reductions; yet major emission reduction scenarios do not sufficiently mitigate relative exposure disparities. Here, we show that without focusing on relative disparity (percent difference) in exposure, the only way to improve air quality and eliminate absolute exposure disparity is to eliminate all emissions (an unlikely outcome). We demonstrate that the relative disparity metric is ethically important and also a controllable societal feature that can reduce absolute disparity in exposure. We illustrate a range of approaches to air pollution policy that go beyond traditional emissions reductions to meaningfully address exposure disparities. These strategies should be at the center of the future U.S. environmental policy

papers.title: Bringing ML to the real world: rewards are all we need
papers.abstract: Realizing the promise of artificial intelligence (AI) to accelerate scientific progress and deliver technological impact depends on how effectively AI can be integrated into real-world decision- making processes. As Peter Norvig states, “Somewhat remarkably, almost all AI research until very recently has assumed that the performance measure can be exactly and correctly specified in the form of a utility or reward function”.1 Once the reward function is known, any problem can be formulated as an optimization or search problem – the areas well explored within the AI community. However, while the long-term objectives of a specific activity are often well defined, constructing short-term rewards that remain aligned with those goals and consistent with real- world constraints remains a major unresolved challenge. Such alignment has been achieved in domains like chess, Go, and supervised machine learning problems, where objectives are well defined and easily simulated. However, no universal solution exists for defining intermediate rewards for complex, evolving scientific goals remains an open challenge. Correspondingly, the key to operationalizing automated instruments, integrating multi-instrument self-driving laboratories, and building geographically distributed research facilities is to generate experiment- aligned probabilistic, domain-specific reward functions. These rewards must be consistent with long-term experimental objectives while remaining actionable on the timescales of decision- making on laboratory tools in microscopy and materials synthesis labs – proper reward definition operationalizes scientific intent. Here, we review the extant reward structures in the physical sciences and summarize opportunities for reward design informed by physical principles, human heuristics, and LLM-based reasoning.

papers.title: Self-assembly of Phenylalanine Oligopeptides: Development, Transferability and Performance of Bottom-up Coarse-grained Potentials
papers.abstract: This study extends a previously reported bottom-up coarse-grained force field targeting the phenylalanine tripeptide. Two new peptide chain lengths are investigated, and only the new degrees of freedom are parameterized, leaving the original force field intact. The transferability and performance of the new force field are analyzed by comparing results from simulations of a single peptide and multiple peptides self-assembling in aqueous solution, with corresponding results obtained using different versions of the Martini force field. The predictions from the new force field are benchmarked against available experimental results.

papers.title: Unveiling Phase Synergy and Heterogeneity in O3-P2 Biphasic Sodium Layered Oxides
papers.abstract: Sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) present a cost-effective and sustainable alternative to lithium-ion batteries, with layered oxide cathodes offering high specific capacity, energy density, and cycle life. Phase engineering along with compositional tuning, plays a critical role in optimizing the electrochemical properties of layered transition metal oxides. In this study, we report a systematic phase-engineering strategy to enhance the electrochemical performance of NaₓMn₀.₅Ni₀.₄Fe₀.₁O₂ (MNF541) through controlled modulation of sodium content (x = 1, 0.85, and 0.65), yielding O3, P2, and O3-P2 biphasic materials. The O3-P2 composite, containing only 13.5% of the P2 phase, exhibited a high reversible capacity of 134 mAh g⁻¹ at C/2, an exceptional coulombic efficiency of 99.91%, and outstanding cycling stability, maintaining 99.7% of its initial capacity after 400 cycles within the 4.0 - 2.0 V window. The biphasic system also exhibited superior rate performance and reduced charge-transfer resistance at all states of charge. When cycled up to 4.3 V, the O3-P2 material outperformed pure O3 in both capacity (>190 mAh g⁻¹) and cycle life, underscoring the pivotal role of minor phase synergy in stabilizing high-voltage operation. Multiscale structural and spectroscopic analyses, including AFM and micro-Raman mapping, revealed the intimate coexistence of O3 and P2 domains within individual O3-P2 particles, along with discrete O3-rich regions that are more prone to structural degradation during cycling. X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) analysis indicated that Ni, Fe, and Mn predominantly exist in +2, +3, and +4 oxidation states, respectively. Ni-centered redox processes dominate below 4 V, while Fe oxidation becomes more prominent at higher voltages, as confirmed by low-temperature Mössbauer spectroscopy. Spatial heterogeneity in Fe oxidation states across the electrode, revealed by micro-XANES mapping and reflected in inconsistencies within bulk XANES spectra, underscores the pivotal role of spatially resolved characterization coupled with low-temperature spectroscopies in capturing the formation and dynamic evolution of transient Fe⁴⁺ species and elucidating their influence on electrochemical performance.

papers.title: Harnessing Electrogenerated Bases for Sustainable Organic Transformations
papers.abstract: Electrogenerated bases (EGBs) are emerging as powerful and sustainable tools in synthetic chemistry, offering cleaner and more efficient alternatives to traditional stoichiometric bases. This Review outlines the fundamental principles of EGB formation and explores their expanding role in enabling diverse and selective organic transformations, including alkylations, trifluoromethylations, Stevens rearrangements, Wittig reactions, esterifications, additions, anionic chain reactions, macrolide formation, polymerizations, C–H deprotonations and functionalizations, condensation reactions, and electrocarboxylation. EGBs efficiently activate substrates bearing labile protons, facilitating the generation of reactive intermediates for key bond-forming steps. These methods enable access to heterocycles, fluorinated compounds, and valuable intermediates relevant to pharmaceuticals and materials science. Beyond expanding synthetic scope, EGBs enhance regio- and stereoselectivity, contributing to greater reaction precision. While batch electrolysis has been widely used, advances in flow electrochemistry offer improved control, safety, and scalability. Innovations such as “ex-cell” reactor designs, where oxidation and reduction steps are spatially separated, further improve efficiency and minimize side reactions. The use of environmentally benign materials—such as electrodes (e.g., magnesium), green solvents, and sustainable electrolytes—significantly influences both performance and sustainability. Despite these advantages, challenges remain, including limited substrate tolerance, sensitivity to reaction conditions, and the requirement for specialized electrochemical equipment.

papers.title: Synthesis of Bulky α-Cationic Phosphines and Their Applications in π-Acid Catalysis
papers.abstract: We have developed a synthetic method for triazolium-based bulky α-cationic phosphines. The influence of the steric properties of these cationic phosphines on the catalytic activity in the platinum-catalyzed hydroarylation of propargyl ethers was systematically investigated, revealing that bulky substituents on the triazolium ring enhance the catalytic efficiency. The combination of platinum chloride and bulky α-cationic phosphines enabled the synthesis of various chromenes, including a BINOL-derived optically active chromene. In addition, bulky α-cationic phosphines proved effective for the gold-catalyzed hydroamination of propargyl amine derivatives. Notably, increasing the bulkiness of substituents on the triazolium ring improved the chemoselectivity toward the exomethylene product.

papers.title: Probing Non-Covalent Interactions in Biomatrices by Native Affinity Capture Mass Spectrometry: Biotransformation of Antibodies Conjugated with Small Molecules and siRNA
papers.abstract: Protein therapeutic complexes, such as interchain cysteine-conjugated antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) and siRNA-based antibody-oligonucleotide conjugates (siRNA AOCs) that form non-covalent antibody subunit assemblies, are increasingly prevalent. Biotransformation assessments of protein therapeutics in complex biomatrices are often conducted using affinity capture coupled with reversed phase liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry under denaturing conditions (AC-MS, for clear distinction refer to as AC-denaturing MS), which allows direct measurement of clipping sites and relative quantification. However, AC-denaturing MS is unsuitable for analyzing the biotransformation of non-covalent protein therapeutics as stability information is lost for the non-covalent component. This manuscript presents a novel biotransformation analysis method that preserves non-covalent interactions by combining affinity capture with neutral pH competitive elution and native size exclusion chromatography–mass spectrometry, named as native affinity capture-mass spectrometry (native AC-MS). The successful recovery of non-covalent complexes, including a cysteine-conjugated ADC mimic molecule and siRNA AOCs in various biomatrices, demonstrates the capability of native AC-MS to maintain non-covalent interactions during characterization. Optimized competitive elution exhibits comparable recovery to standard denaturing elution. Native AC-MS offers sufficient sensitivity (low µg/mL limit of detection for antibody) for in vivo studies, as demonstrated by an in vivo plasma siRNA AOC analysis example. To our knowledge, this is one of the first report of in vivo biotransformation analysis of siRNA AOCs. The method provides valuable information, including relative abundance and metabolite identification and can be widely adapted for biotransformation of non-covalent modalities.

papers.title: Non-Covalent Design Strategies for Topological Switching in acyclic bis-cyclodiphosphazane scaffolds
papers.abstract: Rational control of molecular topology through non-covalent design strategies offers a powerful route to create chemically responsive frameworks in main-group chemistry. However, achieving predictable topological modulation in systems governed by subtle intra- and intermolecular forces remains a significant challenge. Here, we demonstrate that hierarchical non-covalent interactions can be deliberately engineered to dictate both molecular conformation and material behaviour. Hybrid acyclic bis(cyclodiphosphazane) compounds were synthesised via condensation of [ClP(μ-NtBu)₂P(NHtBu)] with hydroquinone (H₂L₁) and 2,5-di-tert-butylhydroquinone (H₂L₂), yielding frameworks 2 and 3, respectively. Compound 2 adopts an S-shaped folded topology stabilised by intramolecular N–H···π arene interactions, whereas oxidation introduces new P=E (E = O, S, Se) acceptor sites that promote intermolecular hydrogen bonding, generating 2a–2c. In contrast, steric hindrance in 3 suppresses folding, favouring a linear topology and weaker P=E···H–C interactions upon oxidation (3a–3c). Together, these systems illustrate how steric and electronic modulation establish a tunable hierarchy of non-covalent interactions, providing a blueprint for designing adaptive, stimuli-responsive main-group frameworks whose chemical and physical properties can be precisely controlled through non-covalent principles.

papers.title: Spontaneous Perovskite Passivator Featuring Dual Functional Groups
papers.abstract: A recent and potent advancement in perovskite solar cells (PSCs) is the emergence of spontaneous heterointerface modulators (SHMs), which bypasses the required additional processes of conventional heterointerface modulations. Among SHMs, alkyl-primary-ammonium-bis(trifluoromethylsulfonyl)imides (RA-TFSIs), used as hole–transport material (HTM) additives, exhibit spontaneous perovskite passivation. Upon deposition of the HTM solution containing the RA-TFSI additive, the RA cations spontaneously passivate the perovskite, exploiting the high adsorption energy of RA cations via its ammonium moiety (NH3+) over the perovskite surface. However, conventional RA-TFSIs passivate only A-site defects in perovskite crystals due to their specific passivation mechanism, which limits their effectiveness and is an intrinsic drawback of RA-TFSIs so far. Moreover, the RA components thus far have been limited; those with multiple functional groups are unprecedented. In this work, we propose a novel strategy for suppressing multiple defect sites using a spontaneous perovskite passivator featuring dual functional groups. 2-thiophene-ethyl-ammonium-TFSI (TEA-TFSI) was newly synthesized and verified as a spontaneous perovskite passivator for n-i-p-structured PSCs employing thermally stable poly[bis(4-phenyl)(2,4,6-trimethylphenyl)amine (PTAA) HTM. Spontaneous perovskite passivation using the TEA-TFSI HTM additive formed a monolayer-like passivation overlayer, unlike that in conventional TEA-based passivators. The TEA cation exhibited dual-site adsorption on A-site and X-site defects via attachments of ammonium and thiophene moieties, respectively, effectively overcoming the single-site limitation of conventional RA-TFSIs. Beyond defect suppression, the TEA overlayer enhanced the physical attachment of PTAA on the perovskite. As a result, the TEA-TFSI HTM additive enhanced the photovoltaic performance of PSCs with thermal stability owing to spontaneous perovskite passivation and thereby achieved power conversion efficiency up to 22.2% and 21.7% for minicells (≈0.12 cm2) and minimodules (≈1.6 cm2, active area: 1.41 cm2), respectively. This study demonstrates a generalizable design principle for multifunctional spontaneous passivators and provides novel insights into SHM engineering for PSCs.

papers.title: Transient and Persistent Effects of Air Exposure on Electrocatalytic Activity of Sub-Nano Pt Clusters on Different Electrode Supports
papers.abstract: Electrodes are exposed to air prior to use in most electrochemistry experiments, but the resulting adventitious contaminants are easily removed by cycling the electrode potential to drive reactions or desorption. In most cases, the resulting changes to the electrode surface are probably inconsequential, however, for electrodes with catalytic centers consisting of sub-nanometer clusters or single atoms, potential cycling may drive dissolution, migration, or other processes that significantly alter the catalyst properties. We have developed the capability to prepare clean electrodes in ultrahigh vacuum, decorated with precisely controlled clusters or atoms, and to study their electrochemistry within the vacuum system after controlled exposures to pure gases or to air. Here, we examine the effects air exposure on the activity for HER, ORR, and oxidation of ethanol and propanol, catalyzed by Pt4 clusters deposited on both ITO and nitrogen-implanted HOPG electrodes. Air exposure was found to have no significant effects on HER but did have substantial effects on the other reactions. Some effects were transient, i.e., they decreased over the course of a few dozen CV cycles, but there were also effects such as increased overpotentials and changes in peak currents or potentials, that persisted after extensive potential cycling.

papers.title: Understanding Synthesis Space in Ligand-Assisted Reprecipitated CsPb(BrxI1-x)3 Perovskite Nanocrystals
papers.abstract: Ligand-assisted reprecipitation (LARP)-based synthetic approach has gained attention as a promising method for scalable synthesis of perovskite nanocrystals (PNCs) with outstanding optoelectronic functionalities. However, such distinct synthetic features of the LARP method involve an intrinsic limitation in realizing red-color emissions from iodine-rich compositions. Herein, we explore the LARP synthesis space of CsPb(BrxI1-x)3 PNCs via a high-throughput robotic synthesis platform integrating machine learning (ML) algorithms, not only allowing for understanding the role of each chemical variable from the multidimensional synthesis space but also refining the bespoke synthesis landscape of PNCs with target functionalities. It is found that ligand ratios as well as the selection of antisolvents dynamically contribute to synthesizing I-rich CsPbX3 PNCs, where their delicate and dedicated adjustments are required depending on the Br-to-I ratios. Furthermore, a disparity between the latent feature in ML-refined synthesis space and the manifested functionality space is identified, where the colloidal nature in the precursor state is found to colligate the bespoke synthesizability and functionality control of the LARP-PNCs. This data-driven approach enables the rational synthetic designs of CsPbX3 PNCs, as well as the fundamental relationship between the synthesis and functionality space, paving a generalizable way to navigate complex synthetic spaces in solution-processed optoelectronic materials.

papers.title: Electronic-Structure Model for a Single Vacancy Defect
papers.abstract: We propose a first-principles electronic structure model for describing a single vacancy defect. Vacancy defects in semiconductors and insulators form color centers, whose localized trap states enable quantum functionalities. The properties of these defect states are affected by their interactions with the surrounding lattice and spin environments. Extensive theoretical efforts have been devoted to understanding such defect-environment couplings within periodic supercell models. While these approaches have provided valuable insights, accurate description of charged defects or nuclear motion associated with electron-phonon coupling requires approaching the dilute-defect limit, which in turn demands prohibitively large supercells and computational cost. Our new model eliminates the artificial periodicity inherent to the supercell model. A single defect is introduced into the pristine crystal under the assumption that the electronic density far from the defect remains nearly identical to that of the pristine system. For the insulating LiH-1D system, this assumption holds well, as neutral and charged defects form localized color centers consistent with the model. In contrast, for the metallic H-1D system, delocalized electronic behavior in charged defects violates this locality condition, limiting the applicability of the approach. We expect that this model can be broadly applicable to investigations of charged color centers and their interactions with the surrounding environment in insulating and semiconducting materials such as diamond, h-BN, transition-metal oxides, and dichalcogenides.

papers.title: Precision Nickel Coating of Complex Nanostructures with Commercially Available ALD Precursors
papers.abstract: Atomic Layer Deposition (ALD) is a scalable, solvent-free synthesis technique that is routinely used for the deposition of thin films with sub-Angstrom precision. The coating of non-planar substrates via particle ALD (p-ALD) can furnish nanoparticle- and single atom catalysts with extreme precision, scalability and reproducibility. Unlike widely explored ALD synthesis of metal oxides and nitrides, however, practical ALD processes for the deposition of non-noble metals remain scarce. Here we show that commercially available nickel hexafluoroacetylacetonate and dimethylamine borane precursors can be used for the deposition of nickel nanoparticles with minimal carbon impurities at 200 °C. Nickel p-ALD on noble metal surfaces such as platinum or gold takes place at only 100 °C, which enables a solvent-free synthesis of core-shell nanoparticles for which the thickness of the Ni shell can be varied with exquisite precision.

papers.title: Octupolar AIEgens Photosensitizers with Enhanced Molar Absorptivity for Near-Infrared Phototheranostics
papers.abstract: High molar absorption coefficients (ε) in the near-infrared (NIR) region are essential for maximizing light-harvesting efficiency, enabling deep-tissue penetration, and enhancing reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation in phototheranostics. However, achieving strong absorptivity at NIR wavelengths remains challenging for organic luminogens due to intrinsically diminished oscillator strengths. Here, we report a symmetry-guided molecular engineering strategy to construct octupolar aggregation-induced emission luminogens (AIEgens) that overcome these limitations. Incorporation of fused tetrahydroxanthylium (THX) acceptors into a D(A)3 framework yields a four-fold enhancement in ε (5.47 × 104 M-1 cm-1) at an absorption maximum of 670 nm compared to dipolar analogues (D-A), while simultaneously achieving bright NIR-II emission at 963 nm. Femtosecond transient absorption (fsTA) spectroscopy reveals stronger ground-state bleaching and additional excited-state absorption bands in octupolar systems, directly correlating with enhanced light-harvesting capacity. Complementary DFT calculations demonstrate that symmetry-enabled dipole coupling activates additional S0→S2 transition channels, rationalizing the unusually high absorptivity. Furthermore, the octupolar architecture reduces ΔEST and introduces additional low-lying excited states, which collectively promote intersystem crossing (ISC) and boost ROS generation. Together, these results highlight a symmetry-driven molecular design strategy in which octupolar architectures with twisted conformations not only preserve AIE characteristics but also achieve unusually high absorptivity, thereby establishing a robust platform for bright NIR-II emission and advanced phototheranostic applications.

papers.title: Click chemistry-based bioconjugates for direct immunochemical analysis of the mycotoxin citrinin
papers.abstract: Immunoassays have been developed for all regulated mycotoxins, including citrinin, whose presence in food supplements has recently undergone additional restrictions in Europe. Immunoassays for mycotoxins most commonly use monoclonal antibodies alongside an enzyme tracer, resulting in the so-called direct antibody-coated competitive ELISA format. Notably, no immunoassay of this kind has been published for citrinin to date. To address this, a novel hapten featuring an azide-functionalised linker for click chemistry conjugation has been designed. Following confirmation by molecular modelling that this derivative is an excellent structural mimic of the mycotoxin, a functional enzyme tracer and an immunising conjugate were prepared and characterised by MALDI-TOF. Subsequently, high-affinity monoclonal antibodies were produced through a double screening process for hybridoma selection. In combination with the click chemistry tracer, these novel antibodies show promise as immunoreagents for setting up innovative direct immunoassays for the sensitive determination of citrinin in food supplements containing fermented red rice

papers.title: Innovative Adaptive Multi-Resolution Modeling Framework for Enhancing Precision, Rigor, and Applicability in Chemical Engineering Research
papers.abstract: This conceptual paper introduces the Adaptive Multi-Resolution Modeling Framework (AMRMF), a novel technique designed to revolutionize chemical engineering by integrating multi-scale simulations, quantum-inspired algorithms, advanced uncertainty quantification, and Bayesian inference. The framework bridges theoretical concepts and experimental applicability, ensuring high precision and rigor across chemical, physical, biological, medical, pharmaceutical, and engineering domains. Through rigorous mathematical derivations, reproducible simulations with Python code, advanced sensitivity analyses, quantitative statistics, uncertainty analysis, and falsifiability assessments, AMRMF enhances productivity, accuracy, and ease in chemical processes, with specific applications in pharmaceutical engineering and integration with digital twin models. Supported by 60 recent references from prestigious journals, this work provides a self-contained theoretical structure without external data dependencies

papers.title: Extremely Long Electron Lifetime in Polycrystalline Perovskite Layer
papers.abstract: Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) are promising next-generation photovoltaics. The high performance of PSCs is attributed to the long carrier lifetimes of perovskite photoabsorbers. However, the carrier lifetimes of polycrystalline perovskite layers, which serve as the photoabsorbers in practical PSCs, have remained limited to several tens of microseconds. Thus, to demonstrate the performance of perovskite photoabsorbers, achieving long carrier lifetimes in polycrystalline perovskite layers is imperative. In this study, a sub-millisecond electron-lifetime of a polycrystalline perovskite layer was demonstrated. This prolonged carrier lifetime was enabled by a combination of a nascent spontaneous perovskite passivation technique, which circumvents exposure of the modulated interface to the atmosphere, and time-resolved microwave conductivity (TRMC) with trap filling via photoexcitation. Under optimal trap filling, with negligible intensity relative to that for the 1 sun condition, a long electron lifetime of up to 547 ± 9 microsecond was achieved for a perovskite layer in the presence of a heterointerface. This is the first observation of carrier lifetime extension in perovskite photoabsorbers via photoexcitation trap filling in TRMC measurements. This study elucidates the effectiveness of emerging spontaneous heterointerface modulation techniques, strengthens characterization techniques for PSC components, and provides helpful guidance for the further development of PSCs.

papers.title: Mechanistic Insights into Layered Growth of Imine-Linked Bilayer 2D Covalent Organic Frameworks
papers.abstract: The crystallinity and stacking order of two-dimensional covalent organic frameworks (2D COFs) are critical to their physical properties and overall performance. However, direct molecular-resolution insight into the growth of layered 2D COFs remains elusive, particularly for imine-linked systems. Herein, we construct imine-linked bilayer 2D COFs at the solid-liquid interface, enabling time-dependent scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) visualization of interlayer growth. STM imaging revealed a layered growth mechanism involving defect-mediated nucleation, lattice-guided directional propagation, cross-defect growth, and oriented domain coalescence. This growth pathway gives rise to local order-on-disorder stacking associated with defect-induced registry variations. These findings provide direct molecular-level visualization of layered growth in imine-linked COFs and uncover a mechanistic origin of stacking disorder in bulk COFs.

papers.title: Teaching Graduate Level Structure–Dynamics Concepts of RNA at the Undergraduate Level using Solution State NMR spectroscopy
papers.abstract: Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR) spectroscopy is a reliable and useful technique for determining the structure and dynamics of ribonucleic acid (RNA) biopolymers. Information on the structure and dynamics obtained can be used to understand an RNA’s function. There are many different types and functions of RNA molecules, such as mRNA, miRNA, siRNA, tRNA, and rRNA. Recent discoveries by and Nobel prizes awarded to scientists have demonstrated just how important RNA is. In the undergraduate curriculum, students are mainly introduced to RNA’s role in protein synthesis. In addition, students are also only exposed to NMR spectroscopy of small molecules in their organic chemistry classes. To expand students' knowledge of RNA and NMR spectroscopy, we have designed a series of lectures to teach upper-level biochemistry/chemistry undergraduate students important skills involved in RNA structure and dynamics determination using NMR spectroscopy, traditionally graduate-level concepts. In the course, we first teach the general theory of NMR and then focus on NMR spectroscopy applied to RNA molecules. Students then process, interpret, and assign 2D Heteronuclear Single Quantum Coherence (HSQC) NMR experiments. This assignment then allows them to identify each uracil in the HIV-2 TAR element RNA structure. Students then process, analyze, and determine the longitudinal (R1) relaxation rate constant and draw conclusions on the flexibility of each uracil. Using the structure and R1 values, students can conclude how structure can impact the dynamics of RNA molecules and how this information can be used for drug or vaccine development. Throughout the practicum, students have access to instructor-made PowerPoints, activities, and manuals that help students actively engage and understand the material. The general learning outcomes of this course are that students will understand NMR spectroscopy of RNA, how it is used to study structure and dynamics, NMR data processing, analysis, and interpretation, and lastly, the importance of this field of research.

papers.title: Benchmarking van der Waals Treatments for Transition Metal Dichalcogenides: NbS2, MoS2, TaS2, WS2, NbSe2, MoSe2, TaSe2, WSe2, NbTe2, MoTe2, TaTe2, and WTe2
papers.abstract: Accurate treatment of van der Waals (vdW) interactions is essential for exploring the potential of transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) in sensing, energy storage, and catalysis. Here, we present a comprehensive benchmark of twelve representative 2H-phase TMDs: NbS2, MoS2, TaS2, WS2, NbSe2, MoSe2, TaSe2, WSe2, NbTe2, MoTe2, TaTe2, and WTe2, using a suite of density functional theory (DFT) approaches. These include the semi-local PBE functional (bare and with D2, D3, D3M, D3+BJD, and D3M+BJD corrections) and six non-local vdW density functionals (vdW-DF, vdW-DF2, vdW-DF-OB86, vdW-DF-OBK8, vdW-DF-CX, and vdW-DF2-B86R). The results reveal that while no single vdW scheme is universally superior, a consistent subset: PBE+D3, vdW-DF-CX, vdW-DF-OB86, and vdW-DF2-B86R, achieves a balanced and physically reliable description. Among these, vdW-DF-CX and vdW-DF2-B86R provide the most accurate and transferable performance, closely followed by the widely used PBE+D3, which remains a practical choice for adsorption and intercalation studies. In contrast, PBE+D2 shows erratic behavior for W- and Ta-based TMDs, while D3M-based corrections systematically overbind and original vdW-DF and vdW-DF2 underbind, leading to inaccurate layer separations. These results establish a clear hierarchy of vdW treatments for TMDs and provide concise, transferable guidelines for future first-principles studies of layered and hybrid materials where dispersive interactions are essential.

papers.title: Immunomagnetic and Immunogold Sandwich Assay for Borrelia burgdorferi detection from blood samples by fsLA-ICP-MS as a proof-of-concept diagnosis of the Lyme Disease
papers.abstract: This article describes a proof-of-concept study of Borrelia burgdorferi qualitative detection from artificial blood samples by fsLA-ICP-MS, following an immunomagnetic separation and immunogold staining, showing great potential for diagnosis of the Lyme Disease (LD). A powerful magnetic separation method was established for B. burgdorferi preconcentration from 10 mL samples and blood matrix elimination, with the use of 300 nm diameter size magnetic nanoparticles (MNPs) conjugated to anti-B. burgdorferi. Qualitative 197Au fsLA-ICP-MS B. burgdorferi detection was demonstrated after bacteria immunogold staining with 3 nm gold nanoclusters (AuNCs) conjugated to another type of anti-B. burgdorferi. The complete sandwich immunoassay was performed in 10-times diluted artificial blood samples spiked with 2·106 bacterial cfu and the specificity was tested against E. coli. Successful qualitative B. burgdorferi detection of 400 cfu deposited was achieved, with 25- and 20- times higher 197Au CPS intensity compared to negative control samples in absence of bacteria and E. coli showing great potential for real cases application.

papers.title: Stereoselective synthesis of spirocyclic-pyrrolo-quinolinones via cascade [4+2] annulation of indole-based chalcones and activated carbonyl compounds
papers.abstract: A straightforward and stereoselective approach has been developed for the construction of pyrroloquinoline derivatives through the reaction of indole-derived chalcones with diverse Michael acceptors, including alkylidene esters/ketones and vinylidene indanones. The transformation proceeds smoothly under mild conditions, displaying good functional group tolerance. Mechanistically, the process involves a [4+2] aza-Michael addition followed by intramolecular cyclization, affording the desired products in good to excellent yields.

papers.title: Hydrophobic force: not attractive but compressive
papers.abstract: Hydrophobic force is a ubiquitous surface force that governs numerous phenomena in daily life and plays a critical role in biochemistry and life sciences. However, its origin and abnormal behaviors have challenged scientists worldwide for over 80 years. A theory based on a macroscopic physical model is proposed, demonstrating that hydrophobic interaction in its nature is not attractive but compressive. The framework of the theory encompasses (1) Revealing that the cavitation between two hydrophobic surfaces is a capillary phenomenon driven by by Laplace pressure (2) Hypothesizing that the cavitation causes two effects simultaneously: (i) inducing the compressive hydrophobic force due to the negative pressure inside the cavity and (ii) enhancing the van der Waals forces by replacing water with the vapor in the cavity as the medium. (3) Establishing a fundamental equation along with a hydrophobic force law enabling the prediction of both the magnitude and decay length of the force. (4) Elucidating the origin of the hydrophobic force at the molecular level with a qualitative model (5) Revealing the unique properties of hydrophobic force such as having upper limits in both magnitude and operational range, violating Derjaguin Approximation and being of a non-equilibrium nature. Critically, the theory is rigorously validated through multiple case studies of direct force measurement experiments published over the past decades, showing strong agreement. Furthermore, it provides coherent explanations for nearly all the open questions regarding hydrophobic force. It is expected that the findings could have a broad impact on the science and technology in the related fields.

papers.title: A Comprehensive Benchmark and Hierarchical Reasoning Prompting for Large Language Models in Engineering Problem Solving Evaluation
papers.abstract: Recent progress in language models has shown great potential, yet their performance in highly specialized engineering fields—requiring strict precision, logical rigor, and nuanced design reasoning—remains insufficiently explored. This work presents EngiBench, a comprehensive evaluation framework designed to systematically assess model capabilities in engineering knowledge, computation, reasoning, and judgment across diverse sub-domains. To improve reliability and interpretability, we propose a Hierarchical Reasoning Prompting (HRP) strategy that mirrors the structured thinking process of human engineers, involving problem decomposition, knowledge application, analytical reasoning, and validation. We further construct EngiBench-QA, a curated dataset of expert-annotated question–answer pairs, along with EngiBench-Mini for human expert comparison. Experimental results show that HRP notably enhances model accuracy and consistency, surpassing conventional prompting and achieving strong alignment with expert-level reasoning. Nonetheless, challenges persist in open-ended design, complex simulation, and managing overconfidence.

papers.title: Aqueous Electrochemical CO₂ Capture with Oxygen-Stable Azopyridine Surpassing Electron-Utilization Limits
papers.abstract: Electrochemically mediated carbon capture (EMCC) in aqueous media offers economic viability but is constrained by poor solubility of redox species and superoxide formation. Here, we demonstrate an oxygen-tolerant EMCC platform using surfactant-assisted 4,4’-azopyridine (AzPy) to enhance solubility and enable super-stoichiometric carbon dioxide (CO2) capture. Experimental and DFT analyses reveal that two-electron reduction of AzPy induces pKa shifts, facilitating the binding of three protons and indirect capture of three CO2. Bulk electrolysis under oxygen (O2) and across varied state-of-charges confirms O2-tolerance with electron utilization up to 150%. Symmetric flow operation in 20% O2 achieves substantially lower energy consumptions of 29.9 and 72.0 kJ molCO2⁻¹ at 15% and 480 ppm CO2, respectively, compared to reported benchmarks. Continuous flow operation further demonstrates simultaneous CO2 capture and release with >100% utilization and a record-low energy of 2.5 kJ molCO2-1. Our study establishes surfactant-facilitated solubility enhancement and electrochemical pKa modulation as robust strategies for efficient aqueous EMCC.

papers.title: Step-Function Shell Model: Algebraic and Quantum Foundations of Periodic Table Period Lengths and Noble Gas Shell Closures
papers.abstract: Building on prior mathematical formulations of the periodic law, this paper demonstrates that the algebraic formula S(k) = 2 * (floor(k/2) + 1)^2 accurately predicts the period lengths (2, 8, 8, 18, 18, 32, ...) of the periodic table. This pattern is not a numerical coincidence but a direct consequence of the fundamental quantum identity governing angular momentum degeneracy, where the sum from l=0 to m-1 of (2l + 1) equals m^2. While this sequence was previously identified as a mathematical regularity by Restrepo and Pachón (2007), its physical and quantum-mechanical origin remained unexplained. Our work provides a rigorous physical derivation by framing the observed sequence within a Step-Function Shell Model. Here, the index m(k) = floor(k/2) + 1 dictates the sequential completion of angular momentum layers, corresponding to well-defined quantum subshell closures. This novel derivation bridges the gap between a known mathematical pattern and its underlying quantum principle, thereby establishing the algebraic structure as a fundamental physical law rather than an empirical curiosity. Notably, the cumulative sum of period lengths, C(k) = sum from j=1 to k of S(j), perfectly reproduces the atomic numbers of all seven known noble gases (Z=2, 10, 18, 36, 54, 86, 118), and extends further to predict future shell closures beyond current empirical observation. These predictions provide clear, mathematically grounded targets for exploring superheavy elements. Our work hence elevates the classical descriptions of periodicity by revealing the quantum-symmetric foundations of the periodic table’s geometry and shell closures. The Step-Function Shell Model comprehensively links the algebraic formula to quantum angular momentum degeneracy and the empirical chemical periodicity in a unified framework that deepens understanding of atomic shell structure and noble gas stability. The model’s simplicity and predictive power advocate its utility in advancing theoretical chemistry and atomic physics research. Furthermore, it suggests explanations for period doubling and multi-period completion phenomena observed in electron shell filling, which are encoded within the eigenvalue structure of angular momentum operators and related quantum symmetries. These results open promising avenues for future theoretical and experimental investigations into atomic shell structure, heavy element synthesis, and quantum-mechanical foundations of chemical periodicity.

papers.title: Machine learning-assisted global life cycle assessment for sustainable biochar design
papers.abstract: Biochar, produced via biomass pyrolysis, is an emerging method for carbon removal in agriculture. However, its uncertain environmental outcomes hinder large-scale adoption. We address this using physics-informed machine learning (ML) to integrate kinetics-based pyrolysis modeling and global datasets of field experiments into dynamic life cycle assessment (LCA). Evaluating biochar derived from 10 types of biomass residues and applied to 4 cropping systems worldwide over 5 years reveals trade-offs between environmental footprints and crop yields. Feedstocks like stimulants and fiber residues boost crop yields but have high climate and environmental burdens (e.g., eutrophication, human health, and ecotoxicity). Feedstock-crop matching is crucial, e.g., circular utilization of maize and soybean residues for biochar applied to the same crops is promising. Our global analysis identifies regions for net carbon-negative biochar-crop systems. Forest residue-derived biochar performs best, while agricultural residues show trade-offs that vary by climate zones and time. This study advances understanding of biochar’s sustainability and offers an ML-LCA tool for large-scale design.

papers.title: Measuring pH inside a bipolar membrane junction
papers.abstract: The local pH environment within bipolar membrane (BPM) junctions is complex and not well understood, yet it is important to control for advancing performance BPM-based electrochemical systems. We report a voltammetric strategy using an ultrathin Ni mesh pH probe to spatially resolve pH variations in the BPM junction during model BPM electrolyzer operation. Under reverse bias, we observe depletion of OH⁻ at the anion-exchange layer (AEL) interface, with the degree of acidification diminishing with increasing distance from the AEL. These gradients correlate with current-dependent water dissociation (WD) and are modulated by the electric field and the surface charge state of the catalyst. By correlating spatial pH profiles with the surface-charging behavior of WD catalysts, we explore a mechanism of catalyst-mediated H⁺ and OH⁻ transfer facilitated by hydrogen-bonding networks. These findings highlight the role of local chemistry and electrostatics in BPM performance and offer new methods to probe and engineer catalytic junctions in electrochemical energy devices.

papers.title: Enthalpy–Entropy Compensation Governs the Solvent-Mixing Effect in Electrochemical Thermoelectric Conversion
papers.abstract: Thermocells convert temperature gradients into electrical energy using the entropy change of a redox reaction. The performance of thermocells is governed by the temperature coefficient of electrochemical potential (α), and the various strategies are reported to increase the α. Among the various strategies, solvent mixing has been recognized as an effective strategy; however, the underlying mechanism remains elusive due to the absence of either systematic experimental or reliable theoretical validation. Herein, we demonstrate that enthalpy–entropy compensation provides a general framework for modeling solvent-mixing effects in thermocells. Variable-temperature electrochemistry reveals the linear relationship between hydrogen-bond entropy (ΔSHB) and enthalpy (ΔHHB) arising from the interactions between methanol and quinone dianions in acetonitrile. This enthalpy–entropy compensation principle enables the prediction of the quinone derivatives with a large entropy change—and consequently a large α value—through DFT-based screening of hydrogen bond enthalpy. Notably, tetramethyl-para-benzoquinone exhibits an α value of −3.1 mV K−1, which is the highest absolute value in liquid-based all-organic thermocells. These findings show that enthalpy–entropy compensation is a general molecular design strategy for creating high-performance thermocells.

papers.title: Decarbonylative Multi-Deuteration of Aldehydes via Sequential Polar and Radical Pathways
papers.abstract: Selective deuterium incorporation offers a powerful means to modulate metabolic stability, and probe reaction mechanisms. However, current methods based on defunctionalization or hydrogen–deuterium exchange are largely limited to mono-deuteration or exhibit poor site selectivity, restricting their utility for accessing multi-deuterated carbons. Developing alternative strategies for site-selective multi-deuteration is therefore highly desirable, as such motifs can further enhance the deuterium kinetic isotope effect (DKIE) and provide valuable opportunities in drug design. Herein, we report a cost-effective method for decarbonylative multi-deuteration of aldehydes, which combines polar α-deuteration, thiyl radical-mediated hydrogen atom transfer (HAT), and subsequent decarbonylation. This method employs inexpensive, commercial sources and features a broad substrate scope including primary, secondary, and tertiary aldehydes, and those in complex settings.

papers.title: Synthesis of α,β-Unsaturated Ketones from Aldehydes and Ketones Using 1,1-Di(boryl)alk-1-enes
papers.abstract: α,β-Unsaturated ketones are important functional groups that are widely used in various fields such as chemi-cal synthesis and molecular biology. Here we report an efficient method for the synthesis of α,β-unsaturated ketones through the boron-Wittig reaction of aldehydes and ketones using 1,1-di(boryl)alk-1-enes as building blocks which are pre-pared from terminal alkynes including propyne. 1,1-Di(boryl)alk-1-enes are deprotonated at the γ-position to generate α,α-di(boryl)allyl anions, which react with aldehydes and ketones at the α-position to give boryl-1,3-dienes. Subsequent oxida-tion of the resulting boryl-1,3-dienes produces α,β-unsaturated ketones. Furthermore, α,β,γ,δ-unsaturated ketones were also synthesized using 1,1-di(boryl)alka-1,3-dienes. The synthetic utility of this method is demonstrated by an application to the concise syntheses of two natural products.

papers.title: Photoinduced Reversible Assembly of Polynuclear Complexes from Ru-Containing Ionic Liquids with Accompanying Ionic Conductivity Modulations
papers.abstract: Solvent-free strategies for constructing coordination assemblies are desirable but remain challenging. We investigated the photochemical reactivity of ionic liquids (ILs) composed of a sandwich-type Ru complex bearing a dialkylaniline ligand, [CpRu(PhNMeC6H13)]+, and cyanoborate anions (B(CN)4–, BEt2(CN)2–, BF2(CN)2–). Upon UV irradiation, these ILs underwent ligand dissociation and formed polynuclear Ru complexes: the B(CN)4 salt yielded a cubane-type tetranuclear complex, whereas the BEt2(CN)2 and BF2(CN)2 salts produced dinuclear species. These structural transformations resulted in a reduction of ionic conductivity by more than one order of magnitude, with full reversibility observed for the B(CN4) salt and near-complete reversibility for the others, which exhibited minor thermal decomposition. In contrast, the IL incorporating a cyanoalkyl-substituted arene ligand, [CpRu(PhC4H8CN)]BF2(CN)2, formed an amorphous, viscoelastomeric coordination polymer and did not exhibit thermal reversibility. This study presents a solvent-free approach for the construction of reversible, photoresponsive ionic assemblies with tunable ionic conductivity.

papers.title: Quaternary Ammonium Salts with B(CN)4 or C(CN)3 Anions: From Ionic Plastic Crystals and Ionic Liquids to Meltable Coordination Polymers
papers.abstract: The effect of the anion shape (tetrahedral B(CN)4− or planar C(CN)3−) on the phase behavior of six synthesized quaternary ammonium salts containing double bonds was investigated. All three B(CN)4 salts formed ionic plastic crystals (IPCs), whereas two of the three C(CN)3 salts formed ionic liquids. The reaction of these salts with their corresponding potassium salts formed meltable coordination polymers (CPs), comprising two- or three-dimensional anionic frameworks bridged by polycyanoanions with incorporated onium cations. Notably, the B(CN)4-based CP with the NMe₃C₂H₃⁺ cation incorporates an unusually large anionic cage unit, [K24{B(CN)4}50]26−, which accomodates 13 cations. All CPs exhibited incongruent melting behavior, where the potassium salt of the anion is deposited upon melting. The C(CN)3-based CPs melted 50–90 K above their parent onium salts, whereas the melting points of the B(CN)4-based CPs and onium salts were comparable, reflecting the high melting points of the B(CN)4 salts, which form the IPC phase.

papers.title: Reaction Mechanisms and Kinetics of OH-Initiated Oxidation of Allyl Cyanide: Atmospheric Relevance and Product Formation
papers.abstract: It is essential to understand the reaction mechanism, kinetics, atmospheric lifetime and global warming potential of allyl cyanide (CH2=CHCH2CN) at the molecular level due to its large-scale applications. In this regard, we have performed a density functional theory (DFT) study of the CH2=CHCH2CN molecule initiated by OH radicals using M06-2X functional combined with 6-311++ G(d, p) basis set. Furthermore, refinement in energetic calculations of all species are done by using higher level of couple-cluster CCSD(T)-FC method along with same basis set. We have explored the potential energy surface (PES) of the H-abstraction reactions by OH radicals as well as OH-addition to the unsaturated C-atoms of the CH2=CHCH2CN molecule. The PES analysis and thermochemical calculations indicate that OH-addition reactions are more dominant than H-abstraction reactions. The rate constants of all the reaction channels are determined using transition state theory (VTST) within the temperature range of 250-500 K. The overall rate constant of the titled reaction was found to be 2.42×10−13 cm3 molecule−1 s−1 at 298 K. The lifetime of the CH2=CHCH2CN molecule is very short due to the reaction with OH radicals and it is estimated as 23 days and 3 weeks. The values of Global warming potentials (GWPs) for the titled compound are found to be 0.019, 0.005 and 0.001 in 20 years, 100 years and 500 years’ time horizons, respectively.

papers.title: Data-driven approach to visualize the correlation between photocatalytic activity and rate constants from excited states
papers.abstract: Even though excited-state properties play a crucial role in photocatalysis, directly correlating these with photocatalytic activity remains challenging. Herein, we propose a method to elucidate the correlations between the catalytic activity of organic photosensitizers and their rate constants of various excited-state processes through integrating machine learning (ML), quantum chemical calculations, and chemical experiments. This approach was applied to interpolative predictions of the yield of the nickel/photocatalytic formation of C–O bonds and radical additions to alkenes using various organic photosensitizers with satisfactory accuracy (R2 = 0.83 and 0.77 on the test set, respectively). The calculated rate constants obtained through quantum chemical calculations proved to be comparable or even superior to the experimentally measured excited-state lifetimes as descriptors. SHAP-based visual analysis revealed that the rate constants corresponding to transitions from the T1 state provide significant contributions to the interpolative prediction of photocatalytic activity. Additionally, the non-radiative decay process between the S1 and S0 states helps describe the low catalytic activity of poorly emissive photosensitizers. These findings highlight the potential of the proposed method to provide insights into photocatalytic properties that are difficult to obtain using conventional approaches.

papers.title: GH172 difructose dianhydride I synthase: A two-stepped journey via glycosylation and cyclization using QM/MM metadynamics
papers.abstract: The difructose dianhydride I synthase/hydrolase αFFase1 catalyzes the reversible transformation of inulobiose into difructose dianhydride I, a compound present in differ ent caramel compositions. The proposed reaction mechanism of such a transformation consists of a glycosylation step followed by a cyclization to yield the dianhydride from the disaccharide. In response to the absence of mechanistical details for the reaction, we made use of extensive hybrid QM/MM metadynamics studies to shed light on the molecular basis of it. Our simulations show that the global reaction for the transfor mation of inulobiose by αFFase1 is slightly exothermic (∆G0 =–1.3 kcal mol−1) in good agreement with the experimental data. Furthermore, we observe that the glyco sylation step is the rate-limiting step of the reaction with an energy barrier of 12.3 kcal mol−1 compared to 8.7 kcal mol-−1 for the cyclization step. Interestingly, our work shows that the–1 sugar of inulobiose changes from an initial E5 conformation into a 4E puckering via the conformational pathway E5 → E5/4T5 → E3 → 4E. Our calculations highlight that in the cyclization step, the three residues E85, K147, and N226 are es sential for the rotation of the +1 sugar in the substrate to facilitate the intramolecular attack of oxygen O1’ to the anomeric carbon. Prompted by these results, we expressed and assayed the N226A αFFase1 variant. Kinetic data confirm an important role for N226 during the cyclization step but are irrelevant for the hydrolysis step.

papers.title: Stimuli Responsive Thiele’s Hydrocarbon Derivatives: Potential Inversion, Strong Electronic Coupling and Influence of Brønsted/Lewis Acids-Bases
papers.abstract: Stimuli responsive diradicaloid systems often display fascinating and tunable electrochemical, optical and magnetic properties. Herein, we present the design and synthesis of a series of nitrogen-containing Thiele’s hydrocarbon (TH) derivatives (2Ph, 2Py and 2Pz), based on phenyl, pyridinyl, and pyrazinyl spacers, with tunable electrochemical, electronic and optical properties. By systematically increasing the number of nitrogen atoms in the molecular backbone, we observed consistent trends in both their absorption and redox properties. A detailed investigation on the different oxidation states of 2Ph, which displays potential inversion, was also performed, including the intermediate radical cationic state (2PhRC). This intermediate represents an intriguing example of a mixed-valent species whose thermodynamic stability, as calculated by the comproportionation constant (Kc), is diminishingly small, whereas the electronic coupling is strong, making it a borderline class II-III mixed-valence compound. External modulation through coordination with Brønsted and Lewis acids reversibly altered the optical responses of 2Py and 2Pz. This work highlights both structural and stimuli-responsive strategies for tuning organic diradicaloid systems, thereby opening new avenues for their applications in functional materials and coordination chemistry.

papers.title: Ring-Opening Arylation of Cyclic Diaryliodoniums via Self-Propagating Aryne Carbomagnesiation
papers.abstract: Cyclic diaryliodonium salts are widely employed as linchpins for the synthesis of functionalized biaryls through ring-opening reactions and as precursors to arynes under basic conditions. Here we uncover a mechanistically distinctive reactivity mode in which aryne generation and arylation are merged into a single, self-propagating sequence mediated by aryl Grignard reagents. The transformation proceeds through a transient cyclic triaryliodane intermediate that undergoes aryne formation and subsequent carbomagnesiation in a self-sustaining cycle. The mechanism, involving key aryne and arylmagnesium intermediates, is corroborated by trapping experiments with both arynophiles and electrophiles. This reaction proceeds with high meta-selectivity for unsubstituted and remotely substituted substrates, while substitution proximal to the aryne moiety can alter the outcome. The process efficiently furnishes iodine-capped teraryl frameworks in high yields across a broad range of aryl Grignard reagents. The transformable C–I bond further renders the products versatile scaffolds for rapid elaboration into complex aromatic architectures.

papers.title: Lattice Oxygen Insertion into CO and CO2 Products during Formic Acid Decomposition on Fe3O4(001)
papers.abstract: We investigated the complex processes occurring with formic acid dehydration and dehydrogenation occurring within the high temperature region (HT2, >540 K) on Fe3O4(001). Our prior study focused on the low temperature region (HT1, <540 K), and found that surface hydroxyl interaction with an embedded formate intermediate, reaction of formate with an oxygen vacancy, facilitate the dehydration reaction and formation of CO. Focusing on the HT2 region, Temperature programmed reaction spectroscopy (TPRS) performed on O18-labeled Fe3O4(001) uncovers the formation lattice oxygen containing CO and CO2 products suggesting intimate participation of the surface. Surface pitting was observed to occur by 700 K in scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) images and arises due to Mars-van Krevelen mediated water and surface oxygen vacancy formation. Repeat TPRS experiments limited to 625 K, such that oxygen vacancies are allowed to accumulate, demonstrate a shift in selectivity away from dehydration and toward dehydrogenation reaction products. The TPRS and STM data suggest a strong connection between surface oxygen vacancies and oxygen incorporation into product species. We propose that within the HT2 region, the accumulation of oxygen vacancies facilitate further oxygen donation to the surface through the formation of doubly-embedded formate species. Through diffusion of the resulting C─H fragment, new C─O bonds are formed leading to lattice oxygen incorporation into the CO and CO2 products. This study not only furthers our understanding of the dehydration and dehydrogenation processes occurring at the Fe3O4(001) surface, but also for heterogeneous metal oxide catalysis.

papers.title: Robust and Sustainable Synthesis of Al-Based MOFs form Waste Aluminium
papers.abstract: Aluminium MOFs have gained researchers attention for their applications in gas sequestration, water harvesting, drug delivery and chemical storage. Current synthetic methods, however, rely on a variety of aluminium salts for synthesis of MOFs within the same family and are not the most efficient sources of aluminium. Herein, we demonstrate a robust synthetic pathway to MOFs CAU-9, CAU-10 (-NO2,-NH2,-N3), CAU-10-py, CAU-15, CAU-21, MIL-53(Al)-TCD, MOF-303 and Al-Fum from aluminium formate, a compound that we have previously synthesized from industrial aluminium waste. We replace commercial aluminium salts with sustainably sourced aluminium, reducing the amount of waste and harmful byproducts, all by using a common aluminium precursor.

papers.title: Highly stable self-assembled nanotubes from a bipyridinium-based amphiphilic pseudopeptide
papers.abstract: Herein, we report an amphiphilic pseudopeptide that spontaneously self-assembles into monodisperse cationic nanotubes under physiological conditions. These nanotubes exhibit fast self-assembly, remarkable thermal stability and thermoreversibility. The self-assembly concentration range is exceptionally broad, enabling the formation of stable hydrogels at concentrations above 5 mM while preserving the nanostructure at micromolar levels.

papers.title: Absolute Binding Affinity of a Phospholipid for a Membrane Protein
papers.abstract: The absolute binding affinity of a ligand determines site occupancy in functional assays and is a critical quantity for elucidating modulatory mechanisms. Established approaches for soluble ligands in enclosed cavities do not translate to lipophilic ligands on hydrophobic surfaces. These limitations impede efforts to resolve lipid-mediated mechanisms in transmembrane proteins. Here, we apply a formally exact computational method (Streamlined Alchemical Free Energy Perturbation, SAFEP) to calculate the absolute binding affinity of an anionic phospholipid for a potential modulatory site on a lipid-sensitive ion channel. Specifically, we calculate the affinity of palmitoyl-oleoyl phosphatidylglycerol (POPG) at a cryo-EM–suggested site on the Erwinia ligand-gated ion channel (ELIC). Within a double-decoupling scheme, we calculate the POPG bulk chemical potential in palmitoyl-oleoyl phosphatidylcholine (POPC)/POPG mixtures and the decoupling free energy from the cryo-EM–suggested site. We extend the restraint scheme of SAFEP to flexible chains and calculate an affinity of -9.7 +/- 0.8 kcal/mol for binding modes in which the glycerol backbone of POPG aligns with the cryo-EM lipid density. This value is consistent with our previous relative binding affinity calculations, while reducing the statistical error by a factor of three and relaxing assumptions required for that calculation. Unbiased simulations reveal that when the backbone is bound, the headgroup can adopt at least two distinct conformations, each interacting with protein residues with established functional implications. The bulk chemical potentials indicate weak non-ideality, showing modest reductions in excess chemical potential at 10–30 mol% POPG; these values can be paired with single decoupling of POPG from any site to avoid recalculating membrane non-ideality. Overall, our results confirm high POPG affinity for this site and demonstrate SAFEP as a tractable route for quantifying absolute lipid–protein affinities for membrane proteins in mixed lipid bilayers.

papers.title: N-Heterocyclic Carbene-Catalyzed Enantioselective Synthesis of Inherently Chiral Pillar[5]arenes
papers.abstract: The catalytic enantioselective synthesis of inherently chiral pillar[5]arene derivatives holds significant promise in materials science, chemical biology, and host-guest chemistry, which is attributable to their unique pillar-shaped architecture. Despite the immense potential, the enantioselective synthesis of pillar[5]arenes remains a formidable challenge.
